posts.text: A tokay is a large, aggressive, nocturnal gecko, and feeding one means working around all three of those facts rather than through them.
posts.title: Feeding A Gecko That Bites Back
alt: A blue and orange spotted tokay gecko on a cork bark wall at night, mid-lunge at a cricket, above a cream band reading Feeding A Gecko That Bites Back.

posts.text: An octopus has three hearts, and the one feeding the body stops beating whenever it swims. Which is most of why they would rather crawl.
posts.title: Three Hearts, One Stops
alt: Photo of a octopus above a cream band reading Three Hearts, One Stops.

posts.text: Jackson's chameleons need gut-loaded insects, careful supplementation, and water they can actually find. Misting is part of feeding, not separate from it.
posts.title: Feeding The Three-Horned Chameleon
alt: A three-horned Jackson's chameleon on a branch with its tongue extended toward a cricket, water droplets on the leaves around it, above a cream band reading Feeding The Three-Horned Chameleon.

posts.text: A sloth can hold its breath underwater for 40 minutes by dropping its heart rate to a third of normal. A dolphin cannot manage that.
posts.title: Out-Holds A Dolphin
alt: Photo of a sloth above a cream band reading Out-Holds A Dolphin.

posts.text: A milk snake is a constrictor that swallows prey whole, which makes prey size and feeding frequency the two numbers that actually matter.
posts.title: What To Feed A Milk Snake
alt: A red, black and white banded milk snake constricting a thawed mouse on aspen substrate, above a cream band reading What To Feed A Milk Snake.

posts.text: A narwhal's spiral tusk is a tooth, up to 10 feet long, and researchers think it senses water temperature and salinity.
posts.title: The Tusk Is A Tooth
alt: Photo of a narwhal above a cream band reading The Tusk Is A Tooth.

posts.text: The California kingsnake earned its name by eating other snakes. Feeding tongs and separate housing are both part of keeping one properly.
posts.title: Why Kingsnakes Get Fed With Tongs
alt: A banded California kingsnake taking a thawed mouse from long feeding tongs inside its enclosure, above a cream band reading Why Kingsnakes Get Fed With Tongs.

posts.text: New Caledonian crows bend hooked tools from twigs to fish grubs out of bark, then pass the technique to their young. That is culture.
posts.title: Crows Teach Tool Use
alt: Photo of a crow above a cream band reading Crows Teach Tool Use.

posts.text: Marketed as a big lizard that eats mice. In the wild it scavenges insects, and that one wrong idea causes more early deaths than any enclosure mistake.
posts.title: Savannah Monitors Do Not Eat Mice
alt: A savannah monitor on packed soil eating a large gut-loaded dubia roach, with a shallow water basin behind it, above a cream band reading Savannah Monitors Do Not Eat Mice.

posts.text: A lyrebird can reproduce chainsaws, car alarms, camera shutters and human voices. One has been recorded doing an entire construction site.
posts.title: It Copies Chainsaws
alt: Photo of a lyrebird above a cream band reading It Copies Chainsaws.

posts.text: Argentine tegus are omnivores, and the adult bowl has more vegetable in it than most new keepers expect going in.
posts.title: What An Adult Tegu Actually Eats
alt: An adult Argentine black and white tegu eating chopped squash and greens from a wide bowl on the floor of its enclosure, above a cream band reading What An Adult Tegu Actually Eats.

posts.text: Tardigrades endure boiling water, deep freezing and the vacuum of space by shutting their metabolism almost entirely off.
posts.title: Survives The Vacuum Of Space
alt: Photo of a tardigrade above a cream band reading Survives The Vacuum Of Space.

posts.text: A green anole is small, quick and cheap, and it will not use a water bowl. Misted leaves are how it drinks.
posts.title: Green Anoles Drink From Leaves
alt: A bright green anole on a broad leaf lapping a water droplet, with a small cricket on the leaf beside it, above a cream band reading Green Anoles Drink From Leaves.

posts.text: A newborn kangaroo is about the size of a grape. It crawls into the pouch and finishes developing there.
posts.title: Born The Size Of A Grape
alt: Photo of a kangaroo above a cream band reading Born The Size Of A Grape.

posts.text: Two tight hides, real clutter, and a water bowl big enough to soak in. Most ball python problems start with an enclosure that feels too open.
posts.title: The Ball Python Setup That Works
alt: Ball python enclosure with hides, clutter, and a large water bowl, above a cream band reading The Ball Python Setup That Works.

posts.text: An electric eel can put out jolts up to 600 volts, enough to stun a horse, and it uses them for hunting and for defense.
posts.title: Six Hundred Volts
alt: Photo of a electric eel above a cream band reading Six Hundred Volts.

posts.text: Hides on both ends, a secure lid, and branches worth climbing. Nearly every corn snake health problem traces back to this setup rather than to luck.
posts.title: Corn Snake Enclosure Basics
alt: Corn snake enclosure with hides, water bowl, and climbing branches, above a cream band reading Corn Snake Enclosure Basics.

posts.text: An owl's eyes are fixed tubes locked into the skull, so it rotates its head up to 270 degrees instead of glancing sideways.
posts.title: Owl Eyes Do Not Move
alt: Photo of a owl above a cream band reading Owl Eyes Do Not Move.

posts.text: Floor space beats height for this one. A real basking area, a hide worth using, and substrate that holds moisture without going swampy.
posts.title: Blue-Tongue Skink Housing
alt: Blue-tongued skink enclosure with basking area, hide, and moisture-retentive substrate, above a cream band reading Blue-Tongue Skink Housing.

posts.text: Reindeer are the only mammals known to change eye color with the season, gold in summer and deep blue in Arctic winter.
posts.title: Eyes That Turn Blue In Winter
alt: Photo of a reindeer above a cream band reading Eyes That Turn Blue In Winter.

posts.text: Height, cover, and branches at every level. A crested gecko in a wide flat tank is using about a third of the space you paid for.
posts.title: Crested Geckos Live Vertically
alt: Vertical crested gecko enclosure with branches, vines, and foliage, above a cream band reading Crested Geckos Live Vertically.

posts.text: A peregrine falcon dives past 240 mph, and tiny bony baffles in its nostrils are the only reason the air pressure does not wreck its lungs.
posts.title: Two Hundred Forty Miles An Hour
alt: Photo of a peregrine falcon above a cream band reading Two Hundred Forty Miles An Hour.

posts.text: Deep substrate is not decoration for this species. A hognose that cannot burrow is a hognose you will rarely see.
posts.title: Hognose Snakes Need To Dig
alt: Western hognose snake enclosure with deep substrate, basking bulb, and hides, above a cream band reading Hognose Snakes Need To Dig.

posts.text: A giant squid's eye runs up to 27 cm across, the largest in the animal kingdom, built for the faintest flicker of light in the deep.
posts.title: Eyes The Size Of Dinner Plates
alt: Photo of a giant squid above a cream band reading Eyes The Size Of Dinner Plates.

posts.text: The greens to insect ratio flips as a bearded dragon grows, and calcium dusting is not optional at any age.
posts.title: What A Beardie Should Be Eating
alt: Bearded dragon eating chopped leafy greens and a calcium-dusted cricket, above a cream band reading What A Beardie Should Be Eating.

posts.text: Bats are the only mammals that truly fly, and many map total darkness by firing up to 200 calls a second and reading the echoes.
posts.title: Two Hundred Calls A Second
alt: Photo of a bat above a cream band reading Two Hundred Calls A Second.

posts.text: Room to climb, dig, hunt and thermoregulate by choice is genuine care. It comes after correct heat and UVB, not instead of them.
posts.title: Enrichment Comes After The Basics
alt: A bearded dragon climbing a sturdy branch inside its enclosure, above a cream band reading Enrichment Comes After The Basics.

posts.text: A flamingo can sleep on one leg because it locks the joint, so holding the pose costs no muscle effort at all.
posts.title: The One-Leg Trick
alt: Photo of a flamingo above a cream band reading The One-Leg Trick.

posts.text: Discus eat in the middle of the water column and leave a mess, which is exactly why the water change routine matters more than the gallon number.
posts.title: Feeding Discus Without Fouling The Tank
alt: Discus fish feeding on frozen bloodworms near the middle of the water column, above a cream band reading Feeding Discus Without Fouling The Tank.

posts.text: A giraffe's neck holds exactly seven vertebrae, the same count as a human neck, just enormously stretched out.
posts.title: Seven Neck Bones, Same As You
alt: Photo of a giraffe above a cream band reading Seven Neck Bones, Same As You.

posts.text: Tall and laterally flattened is an unusual shape for a community fish, and it drives nearly every decision in the tank.
posts.title: Angelfish Need Height, Not Length
alt: Tall angelfish aquarium with driftwood, broadleaf plants, and visible filtration equipment, above a cream band reading Angelfish Need Height, Not Length.

posts.text: Sea otters have the densest fur on earth. With no blubber at all, that trapped air is their only insulation.
posts.title: A Million Hairs Per Inch
alt: Photo of a sea otter above a cream band reading A Million Hairs Per Inch.

posts.text: Filtration, aeration and predator netting are the real build. The fish is usually the smallest number in the whole budget.
posts.title: Koi Keeping Is Pond Keeping
alt: Outdoor koi pond with visible filtration, aeration, and predator netting, above a cream band reading Koi Keeping Is Pond Keeping.

posts.text: Komodo dragons do not kill with dirty mouths. They have real venom glands that stop clotting and crash blood pressure.
posts.title: A Bite That Will Not Clot
alt: Photo of a komodo dragon above a cream band reading A Bite That Will Not Clot.

posts.text: A $10 fish that lives as long as a dog and rearranges the tank for fun. The filtration is where the money goes.
posts.title: The Oscar Tank Nobody Budgets For
alt: Tiger oscar fish swimming in a large, heavily filtered aquarium, above a cream band reading The Oscar Tank Nobody Budgets For.

posts.text: Platypus mothers sweat milk through patches of skin on the belly, and it pools in grooves for the babies to lap up.
posts.title: Milk Without Nipples
alt: Photo of a platypus above a cream band reading Milk Without Nipples.

posts.text: Five gallons, heated, gently filtered, planted. Almost every common betta illness traces back to water quality or temperature.
posts.title: A Betta Needs A Heater
alt: Heated five gallon betta tank with a sponge filter, plants, and a hide, above a cream band reading A Betta Needs A Heater.

posts.text: Hummingbirds fly backwards on a shoulder joint that rotates a full circle, and at night they cut their heart rate by up to 95 percent.
posts.title: The Only Bird That Flies Backwards
alt: Photo of a hummingbird above a cream band reading The Only Bird That Flies Backwards.

posts.text: Guppies are hardy right up until the water slips. A planted 10 gallon with gentle sponge filtration is the setup that keeps them that way.
posts.title: The Planted Guppy Tank
alt: A planted 10-gallon guppy tank with gentle sponge filtration and warm lighting, above a cream band reading The Planted Guppy Tank.

posts.text: The quokka's famous smile is just the shape of its mouth. Mothers can also pause a pregnancy mid-development when food runs short.
posts.title: It Is Not Actually Smiling
alt: Photo of a quokka above a cream band reading It Is Not Actually Smiling.

posts.text: Those barbels are for sifting. Sharp gravel wears them down, and a cory without barbels cannot forage properly.
posts.title: Corydoras Need Sand, Not Gravel
alt: A corydoras catfish tank with soft sand substrate and a school foraging near the bottom, above a cream band reading Corydoras Need Sand, Not Gravel.

posts.text: A shoebill stands motionless for hours, then strikes fast enough to snap a lungfish in half with a bill built for slicing.
posts.title: The Statue That Hunts
alt: Photo of a shoebill above a cream band reading The Statue That Hunts.

posts.text: Solid flooring, a heat source, a hide, and a big solid wheel. The temperature rule is the one that is not negotiable.
posts.title: Hedgehog Cages Cannot Run Cold
alt: Hedgehog enclosure with solid flooring, a heat emitter, hideout, and exercise wheel, above a cream band reading Hedgehog Cages Cannot Run Cold.

posts.text: Meerkat mobs post a sentinel on a raised mound and swap the job about every hour so everyone gets to forage.
posts.title: The Lookout Shift Rotates
alt: Photo of a meerkat above a cream band reading The Lookout Shift Rotates.

posts.text: They are arboreal, so vertical space matters far more than floor space. A sleeping pouch and a safe wheel finish the setup.
posts.title: Sugar Gliders Need Height
alt: Sugar glider cage with tall vertical climbing space, a sleeping pouch, and an exercise wheel, above a cream band reading Sugar Gliders Need Height.

posts.text: An aye-aye taps bark eight times a second, listens for the hollow spot, and hooks the grub out with the same skeletal finger.
posts.title: The Finger That Finds Grubs
alt: Photo of a aye-aye above a cream band reading The Finger That Finds Grubs.

posts.text: Tall, solid-floored, and cool enough for a heat-sensitive species. And built for a pair, because a single degu is the wrong plan.
posts.title: The Degu Cage Is Built For Two
alt: Tall multi-level degu enclosure with ramps, a solid wheel, and a wooden nest box, above a cream band reading The Degu Cage Is Built For Two.

posts.text: A toucan's bill is over a third of its body surface, and by adjusting blood flow it dumps four times its resting heat production through it.
posts.title: The Bill Is A Radiator
alt: Photo of a toco toucan above a cream band reading The Bill Is A Radiator.

posts.text: Height, climbing space, and sleeping pouches. Same shape of setup as a sugar glider, for an animal that is not related to one at all.
posts.title: Housing A Flying Squirrel
alt: Flying squirrel cage with tall vertical climbing space, sleeping pouches, and an exercise wheel, above a cream band reading Housing A Flying Squirrel.

posts.text: Giant manta rays have the largest brain relative to body size of any fish, and in mirror tests they blow bubbles while watching themselves.
posts.title: The Ocean's Biggest Brain
alt: Photo of a giant manta ray above a cream band reading The Ocean's Biggest Brain.

posts.text: Hammocks, ramps, and a litter box they will actually use. Ferrets sleep hard and play harder, and the cage has to do both.
posts.title: The Multi-Level Ferret Cage
alt: Multi-level ferret cage with hammocks, ramps, and a litter box, above a cream band reading The Multi-Level Ferret Cage.

posts.text: A fennec's ears reach 15 cm on a two kilogram animal, packed with shallow blood vessels that dump heat straight into the air.
posts.title: Ears That Work As Radiators
alt: Photo of a fennec fox above a cream band reading Ears That Work As Radiators.

posts.text: Hamsters burrow. Deep bedding, a solid wheel with no rungs, a hide, and a sand bath is the setup that stops most behavior problems.
posts.title: Deep Bedding Changes Everything
alt: Hamster enclosure with deep bedding, a solid exercise wheel, a hideout, and a sand bath, above a cream band reading Deep Bedding Changes Everything.

posts.text: A cassowary's inner toe carries a claw over 4 inches long. Despite the reputation they are shy fruit eaters that would rather leave.
posts.title: The Dagger Toe
alt: Photo of a cassowary above a cream band reading The Dagger Toe.

posts.text: Constant hay, fresh vegetables for the vitamin C they cannot make, and far more floor space than the pet store box suggests.
posts.title: Guinea Pig Cage Essentials
alt: Guinea pig cage with hay rack, water bottle, and fresh vegetables laid out, above a cream band reading Guinea Pig Cage Essentials.

posts.text: The kakapo is the only flightless parrot alive and the heaviest, nocturnal, and males boom a call that carries for miles.
posts.title: A Parrot That Forgot To Fly
alt: Photo of a kakapo above a cream band reading A Parrot That Forgot To Fly.
